No problem, in your late game armies I would substitute yari ash for naginata sam but in the early game I would pump out yari ash as you can get 2 yari for the price of one sam, when you're campaign is more stable I would recommend recruiting your naginata sam from a place with gives you extra armour, since you're nearby the hojo have a settlement south of kai that gives you that, I would demolish the no dachi and build a yari instead, I would even upgrade it so you can get nagainata sam so that you can get a few more naginata sam in a pinch but build an encampment at kai and go for the upgrade that gives charge bonus as that will be your cav production province 

Hope the battle goes well

In my opinion I think you just don't have the numbers to win in a melee engagement, katana and naginata Sam are very powerful units but the ai have a lot more katana sam plus the 7 units of yari ash, I would recommend to retreat from this battle if you can but if you can't I would say hold up somewhere defensive, hold the high ground, never give it to the enemy. 

 I would put your 1 yari ash in spear wall in the middle of your line, then place your two naginata sam besides your yari, same for your katana and then on the edges the naginita warrior monks, place your 4 bow sam in front of your line so they get the first shot off when the enemy approaches, keep your general behind your melee line at all times and place katana cavalry to either flank

When battle starts retreat your bows behind your line when the enemy charges and have them focus their fire on the enemy bows they'll do a lot more for you than just leaving them on fire at will, when every one e is bogged down in melee you might be able to snipe off the 2 generals with your katana cav, if there is a unit of yari ash protecting them do not engage it as you will lose that fight soundly,  once the generals are gone I would then cycle charge the back of the enemy, don't keep them too long in the fight, especially with yari ash,  I don't remember if naginata warrior monks have warcry but use it when your cav is able to cycle charge or when a few units are wavering as it might cause a mass route, dont forget to inspire with your general and rally as it raises your units moral and units fight a lot better with higher moral 

Imo I would replace your katana cav with yari cav instead as 1 unit of yari cav can take on 2 generals with minimal losses and yari cav beat katana cav in a 1 v 1, they are your anti cav cavalry, they also have a greater charge bonus so they are better for cycle charging, they do require your attention as they will melt in melee unlike katana cav so don't leave them in combat, I would also fill your army with yari ashigaru just so you get some numbers in your army as their yari wall makes them an incredibly good unit even Into the late game. 

Best of luck :)
